The remnants of a prior cold front extend southwest into the region 
from beyond 25N160E to just east of the northern CNMI, where they 
interact with an approaching surface trough. This is leading to 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms across Tinian and Saipan
waters. Models show this pattern will hold into at least Saturday, 
as the surface trough gradually crosses the Marianas and the weak 
convergence boundary fragments and shifts west, maintaining most of 
the showers and thunderstorms near Saipan and Tinian the next few 
days. For Guam, scattered island-effect showers and isolated 
thunderstorms remain in the forecast for the afternoon hours of 
Friday and Saturday as winds are expected to be light to gentle out 
of the north to northeast on Friday, and light and variable Saturday.
The likelihood and strength of island-effect showers will depend on 
nearby convection and daytime cloud cover, which would diminish 
diurnal island heating. Earlier this afternoon, island showers 
developed just off the eastern shores of Guam and spread over 
southern portions of the island, but were much diminished compared to
yesterday due to lingering cloud cover in the mid- and upper levels 
of the atmosphere. Early next week, the monsoon trough which extends 
across much of Micronesia looks to flex slightly north toward the 
Marianas, which could bring better shower chances for Guam at times, 
mainly around Monday and Tuesday.

Marine/Surf...
Light to gentle northerly winds will continue for the next day or 
so, gradually veering easterly, then southerly heading into the 
weekend as a trough crosses the islands. Winds will be variable at 
times through the next few days, eventually becoming gentle to 
moderate easterlies late Sunday through early next week. Combined 
seas will be 3 to 4 ft through the next few days, comprised of a 
combination of swells out of the southwest, east-northeast, and 
southeast. For Tinian and Saipan, scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms are expected through Saturday, from convergence along 
the remnants of a prior cold front, interacting with an approaching 
surface trough. For Guam, scattered island-effect showers and 
isolated thunderstorms are expected Friday and Saturday afternoon if 
skies remain sufficiently clear. Additionally, there will be a low 
risk of rip currents along all reefs through at least Friday night.

Tropical Systems...
Invest 92W continues to move away from the Marianas and Micronesia. 
It is now out of the Guam Area of Responsibility (AOR) near 16.0N 
129.8E. 92W looks to continue to develop as it moves closer to the 
Philippines. The invest is now the subject of a Tropical Cyclone 
Formation Alert (TCFA), meaning it is expected to become a 
significant tropical cyclone within the next 24 hours. This is the 
last time Invest 92W will be discussed. For continuing information 
on Invest 92W and the TCFA, see bulletins issued by the Joint Typhoon
under WMO headers ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

Invest 93W is now centered north-northeast of Kwajalein near 13.8N 
169.7E. 93W remains sub-low as it continues to slowly move west with 
little change in intensity or organization. Convection remains 
limited as well. Latest model guidance shows 93W slowly dissipating 
as it moves west, toward the Marianas, over the next few days. 93W 
will be monitored closely over the next few days for any indication 
that this will change. Stay up to date on forecasts and discussions.

Eastern Micronesia...
Only a couple of changes were made to the previous forecast. The 
main change is in the short term, delaying the onset of scattered 
showers another 12 hours as the convection associated with the 
monsoon flow remains south of the forecast points. Otherwise, expect
increased showers, with POPs (Probability of Precipitation) 
remaining in the 30 to 50 percent range through the beginning of next
week. Overall, Pohnpei and Kosrae can expect to see an unsettled 
pattern beginning Friday morning. Majuro looks to remain fairly dry 
through the weekend, with increasing showers early next week.

Marine conditions will be unchanged, with seas remaining at or below
5 feet and mostly light to gentle winds through the period.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery late this afternoon continues to show isolated to 
scattered showers around the three forecast points with a monsoon 
trough spanning across western Micronesia. Isolated thunderstorms are
also observed northeast of Yap and are being supported by upper-
level divergence. Low-level convergence around Chuuk will bring 
increasing shower and thunderstorm chances starting tonight and 
continuing through much of the weekend. The aforementioned area of 
isolated thundestorms and higher-end scattered showers east/northeast
of Yap is expected to push westward into Yap on Friday and persist 
through much of Saturday. Drier weather is expected to prevail at 
Palau with shower coverage topping out at low-end scattered.
